chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you pray behind an Imam whom you do not follow, recite behind him, whether you hear his recitation or do not hear it.

key_terms.لَا تَقْتَدِي بِهِ: Do not follow (in terms of Imamate/following school)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to recite Surah Al-Fatihah when praying behind a Non-Shia Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of *qira'ah khalf al-imam* (recitation behind the Imam), establishing that the follower must recite Surah Al-Fatihah independently even when praying behind a Non-Shia Imam, regardless of audibility. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the individual obligation of recitation as a pillar of prayer, distinct from the Hanafi view where recitation is often omitted behind an Imam in silent prayers. It underscores the theological principle that the validity of the follower's prayer relies on their own fulfillment of the essential acts, rather than mere imitation of the Imam's actions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you pray a Salāt behind a Imam you do not follow with (a Non-Shia), so recite behind him, whether you can hear his recitation or cannot hear it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When you perform Salah (prayer) behind an Imam who is not qualified, read behind him the recitation, regardless, you hear him or not.’”
